title: No terminal status exists for duplicate/superseded/wont-do work, so retiring one falsely implies work happened
description:
Measured independently by three sessions during the 2026-09-17 fleet-wide dedupe pass (OPAG-176), converging without coordinating: opum-agent, opum-cli-e2e, and this session all hit the same wall retiring a never-worked duplicate.

MEASURED HERE directly, not relayed: `quest task status-flow --json` reports statuses ["To Do","In Progress","Done"], terminalStatuses ["Done"], pausedStatus "Paused". Only "Done" is terminal. `quest task edit <id> --status Done` from "To Do" is refused:

  {"error_type":"validation","message":"Illegal task transition: To Do -> Done.","principal":null}

So retiring a task that was never worked (a duplicate found before anyone touched it, a stale premise overtaken by events) requires stepping it through "In Progress" first -- a status whose entire meaning elsewhere in this schema is "someone started this." Used this exact workaround five times in this pass (QCLI-259, 97, 200, 201, plus historically QCLI-287-adjacent work); each time added an explicit finalSummary sentence stating the In Progress step was not a claim that work happened, because the status field itself cannot say that.

This is not a workflow question to relearn per-session -- it is a schema gap. Two independent repositories (opum-agent, opum-cli-e2e) reached for the same Done+RESOLVED-AS-DUPLICATE convention without coordinating, each writing compensating prose into finalSummary because the status field could not carry the distinction. A convention held up by prose in every closing task is a process patching over a missing mechanism.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A decision is recorded on the shape: a new terminal status (e.g. Wont-Do or Superseded) alongside Done, vs. a status-independent disposition field/flag on an already-Done record, vs. an explicit reason to keep the current two-status workaround
If a new terminal status or field is added, quest doctor and task status-flow surface it so a future session does not have to rediscover the To-Do-to-Done refusal by hitting it

Existing records that used the In-Progress-then-Done workaround (at minimum QCLI-259, QCLI-97, QCLI-200, QCLI-201 in this repository) are not required to be retroactively rewritten -- prospective only, matching this fleets own converged position on the priority/type vocabulary question (QCLI-330)
The decision and its reasoning are documented somewhere a future retiring session will read before reaching for the same workaround

plan: 1. Domain: LifecyclePolicy gains closedStatus (default "Closed"), a terminal status OFF the ladder, reached only by quest task close and legal from To Do, In Progress and the paused status. The record gains resolution {kind: duplicate|superseded|wont-do, survivor?}: survivor is required for duplicate and superseded, and refused for wont-do and for the task itself.

2. Application and CLI: quest task close <id> --resolution <kind> [--survivor <id>] [--final-summary] moves the record to completed/ (kind task.closed). The survivor must resolve to an existing task. demote out of Closed clears the resolution. task edit --status Closed is refused, naming task close.

3. Surfacing (AC2): status-flow lists Closed in terminalStatuses and adds closedStatus and resolutions. doctor reports a closed record with no or invalid resolution, a missing survivor, and a resolution on a non-closed record, and never rewrites any of them. The To Do -> Done refusal names quest task close.
4. Consumers inside quest read terminal membership, never a Done literal: readiness, board, overview, list, milestone closure.
5. Prospective only (AC3): no migration, and the workaround records are untouched.
6. Docs (AC4): the task-finalization and overview guides say when to close versus complete. The CHANGELOG Unreleased entry is marked breaking, so the pair takes a minor bump per the ADR.
7. Proof: tests in both directions plus a predicted-subset mutation, bun run check, lore check. Consumer sweep of sibling repos in two passes. lore-cli is told it owes a hardcoded-Done check.
implementationNotes: Ruled by opum-doc ADR add-a-second-terminal-task-status-for-duplicate-superseded-and-wont-do-outcomes, read by ref at opum-doc main b4f4057 (dev is the same commit). The ADR leaves the status name to quest-cli and uses "Closed" as a placeholder. I am keeping "Closed". Paired with a REQUIRED resolution, it asserts that the task is terminal and never that the work was done, and `quest task close` reads naturally beside `quest task complete`. Rejected: "Retired", because it collides with the retired-paused-literal vocabulary already in tasks.ts; and "Wont Do", because that is one of the three resolution values.

SHAPE: RULED B NOW, A LATER. opum-agent's final ruling, recorded as ODOC-315: an amendment to the ADR, read by ref at opum-doc main == dev == d6516c5 ("Amendment: rollout shape"). It supersedes that session's brief ruling for A. The reason, verified at lore-cli 640195ec and in v0.11.0: lore's statusFlow() throws drift when terminalStatuses is not a subset of statuses (src/adapters/quest.ts:676-681). It runs inside probe() (:405), which ensure() awaits before every adapter operation, so shape A would break every tracker-touching command of every published lore. opum-cli-e2e suites/21-quest-records.mjs:37-39 (5988da75) asserts the same subset. The A step is filed as QCLI-406 (#385, f5dc4b1).

BUILT (implementer specialist, commit 9c0ef51, reviewed here):
- `quest task close <id> --resolution duplicate|superseded|wont-do [--survivor <id>] [--final-summary]`, envelope kind task.closed. The record moves to completed/ with resolution {kind, survivor?}.
- Exit codes: 2 for bad or missing --resolution and for survivor rule violations; 3 for a missing survivor; 6 for a survivor that is the task itself, or a task already Done or Closed.
- Legal from To Do, In Progress, Paused, and retired Blocked. Blocking gates do not hold it.
- status-flow data: terminalStatuses ["Done"] unchanged; closedStatus "Closed" and resolutions added.
- Doctor: task_resolution_invalid, task_resolution_survivor_not_found.
- Readiness treats Closed as terminal.
- `task list --status Closed` works.
- Demote out of Closed withdraws the resolution.
- The To Do -> Done refusal names task close.
- Guides updated. CHANGELOG under ### Added (non-breaking: no existing command, field or exit code changes).

VERIFIED HERE, independently of the implementer's run:
- bun run check exit 0, 920 pass, 0 fail.
- lore check 0.
- Live `task status-flow --json` returns {statuses:[To Do,In Progress,Done], terminalStatuses:[Done], pausedStatus:Paused, closedStatus:Closed, resolutions:[duplicate,superseded,wont-do]}.
Implementer's measurements (their run):
- test/qcli331-closed-status.test.ts has 24 tests. Against the pre-change src, 22 fail and 2 pass; the 2 are the byte-stable and Done-demote regression guards.
- Mutating survivor-required to if(false) was predicted to turn 2 red, and exactly those 2 went red.
- All 403 records in this repo's .quest/ round-trip byte-for-byte.

JUDGEMENT CALLS, recorded for review:
(1) The advertised manifest `fields` for task status-flow and task view were left unchanged. The implementer did this because quest's OWN tracker adapter (src/contract/tracker/index.ts probe) matches them exactly. I checked lore-cli 640195ec: its REQUIRED_COMMANDS checks name, kind and mutating only, and `fields` appears nowhere in src/adapters/quest.ts. So lore would tolerate advertising them. The manifest therefore under-advertises closedStatus/resolutions/resolution. That is a small follow-up, noted on QCLI-406.
(2) Resolution shape is enforced at WRITE time plus doctor, not at read time, so that one hand-edited record cannot make every command unreadable.
(3) A dependency closed as wont-do satisfies readiness. This follows the ADR's terminal semantics, but whether "won't happen" should unblock dependents is worth a design look.
(4) Closing an archived To Do task moves it to completed/.
(5) Not covered by a test: that gates do not block close.

KEY-SET CHECK, 2026-09-28, at the orchestrator's request. opum-cli-e2e described `task close` as returning "a new top-level resolution field on the success envelope". If that were literal, it would breach the envelope index rule (CLAUDE.md constraint 4: contractVersion at index 1, and additive keys only after data and before principal). I MEASURED it on quest-cli dev 999a730 in a realpath'd temp workspace: T-1 created as the survivor, T-2 closed with `quest task close T-2 --resolution duplicate --survivor T-1 --json`, exit 0.
- `jq keys_unsorted` gives ["schemaVersion","contractVersion","kind","data","principal"], identical to the `task complete` control envelope from the same run.
- `has("resolution")` at the top level gives false.
- `[.data.status, .data.resolution]` gives ["Closed",{"kind":"duplicate","survivor":"T-1"}].
Verdict: `resolution` is a key of the RECORD under data, not an envelope key. No constraint is breached and no change is needed. The e2e phrasing named the record's new field, not an envelope key. To re-check: `quest task close <id> ... --json | jq keys_unsorted`.
finalSummary: Added a second terminal status, Closed, reached by `quest task close --resolution duplicate|superseded|wont-do [--survivor <id>]`. It retires never-worked work directly from To Do, In Progress or Paused, without borrowing In Progress or asserting Done. The shape is B now, A later (ODOC-315 amendment, opum-doc d6516c5). status-flow reports closedStatus and resolutions beside an unchanged terminalStatuses, because every published lore drifts on a terminal status outside `statuses`. Moving Closed into terminalStatuses is QCLI-406. Doctor reports inconsistent resolution shapes without rewriting them. The To Do -> Done refusal names task close. The guides say when to close rather than complete. The change is prospective; old workaround records are untouched. Verified: 24 new tests, red-before (22/24) and a predicted-subset mutation (2/24), bun run check 920/0, lore check 0, live status-flow read.
